definition: A standardized document accompanying a released model that describes its intended uses, limitations, training data, and evaluation results.
details: Model cards promote transparency by giving downstream users and developers the information needed to assess whether a model is appropriate and safe for their intended use case.
story: Picture guardrails on a mountain road — not there to slow you down on the straightaways, but to keep you from flying off the cliff. Think of it this way: A standardized document accompanying a released model that describes its intended uses, limitations, training data, and evaluation results. And here is the clever part: Model cards promote transparency by giving downstream users and developers the information needed to assess whether a model is appropriate and safe for their intended use case. It is the difference between “it works” and “it is safe to put in front of people.” And that is Model Card — the reason we can move fast without breaking things, or people.
